source_title: In His 1995 Most Beautiful Interview, Patrick Stewart Shared How Baldness Led to His Big Break at 47 - People.com
source_excerpt:
Stewart was best known for his portrayal of Captain Picard in the ‘Star Trek’ franchise
Stefanie Keenan/Getty; CBS Photo Archive/Getty
Patrick Stewart played Captain Picard for seven seasons of Star Trek: The Next Generation and four films
He recalled that creator Gene Roddenberry initially thought he was wrong for the role
Stewart returned as Picard in 2020 for the Paramount+ series Star Trek: Picard
Patrick Stewart was cast in his most iconic role in middle age — and losing his hair helped get him there.
Stewart, who died at age 86, was a prolific actor known for his work in theater, film and television — but most famously for his portrayal of Captain Picard in the Star Trek franchise, a role he landed later in life.
The actor was 47 when he finally got his big break on Star Trek : Next Generation, starring as Captain Picard on all seven seasons and reprising the character in four Star Trek films from 1994 to 2002.
He returned to the role in 2020 on the Paramount+ series Star Trek: Picard .
Speaking to PEOPLE for its 1995 Most Beautiful issue, the actor said that he was appalled when he began losing his hair at age 19. It was through acting, he said, that he found a chance “to hide myself.”
In an interview with PEOPLE in March 2022, the actor recounted how his first audition for the role in Star Trek seemingly did not go well.
“My first interview [with Star Trek creator] Gene Roddenberry lasted all of about six minutes,” he said. “I learned afterward that when I had gone out the door, he said, ‘Who the hell suggested inviting that guy to come up here? What a waste of time.’”
He continued: “Six months later I was offered the role. Gene thought I was completely wrong, but he was outvoted. I knew a few people in the industry, and all of them except one said, ‘Patrick, look, it’s not going to work out. You cannot revive an iconic show like Star Trek . You’ll be lucky to make it through the first season.’”

Stewart had been acting for decades prior to landing the role and, according to his official website , received a full grant to the Bristol Old Vic Theatre School in 1957, making his onstage debut as Cutpurse in its production of Cyrano de Bergerac in 1959. His first on-screen credit came in 1967 as a fire officer on Coronation Street , and his Broadway debut just four years later, playing Snout in A Midsummer’s Night Dream .
Stewart’s longtime spokesperson, Kelly Bush Novak, said in a statement on Thursday, Oct. 29, “We announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia.”
“He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter, and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all. We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace.”
